title: The absolute Gabber modification and its four-stage construction
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be an integral Noetherian quasi-excellent separated fs log regular scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Quasi-excellence of a scheme means that every affine open has quasi-excellent coordinate ring; separated means its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is closed. Let a finite group $G$ act by log automorphisms, tamely and generically freely: geometric-point stabilizers have order invertible in their residue fields, and the action is free on a dense invariant open. Write $Z$ for the complement of the log triviality locus and $F$ for the complement of the largest free open.

There is a choice, simultaneously for these triples, of a finite normalized blowup tower $b:X^*\to X$, equivariant for $G$, projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and an isomorphism over $X\setminus(Z\cup F)$. Normalized blowup means ordinary blowup followed by normalization in the common function field. The source is integral and fs log regular, with boundary $b^{-1}(Z\cup F)$ and a very tame action. Very tame means that each geometric inertia group acts trivially on the characteristic monoid and on $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X^*,\bar x}/I_{\bar x})$, where $I_{\bar x}$ is generated by nonunit log sections [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and its order is invertible at $\bar x$.

The tower can be chosen as the following four-stage procedure. The first stage is a $G$-equivariant saturated log blowup tower making the source regular. The second is the boundary-stratum blowup tower making the boundary strict normal crossings and $G$-strict, where $G$-strict means that distinct translates of any boundary component are disjoint. Both stages are saturated log blowup towers. Strict normal crossings means a reduced divisor on a regular scheme with regular distinct components whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have codimension $r$. The third is the finite $G$-equivariant permissible fixed-locus blowup procedure: repeatedly blow up the nonempty minimal fixed subschemes and their strict transforms, replacing the boundary by its strict transform together with the exceptional divisor. Permissible means the center is locally cut out by a subset of regular parameters in which the boundary is a product of distinct parameters. This stage makes inertia abelian and the action free outside the boundary. Locally its operations are the fixed-locus blowups of X 1.4--1.7. The fourth is the abelian-inertia rigidification construction of VIII 5.3.8--5.5.5: enlarge the boundary locally to a very tame strict normal crossings boundary, resolve its quotient by functorial saturated log blowups, pull back in fs log schemes, and retain only the inverse image of the original boundary. This construction is independent of the auxiliary enlarged boundary and is compatible with strict inertia-preserving morphisms, so the local fourth-stage modifications glue. Strict means the source log structure is pulled back from the target; inertia-preserving means an isomorphism on geometric stabilizers.

If $X$ is quasi-projective of finite type over an affine Noetherian scheme $B$, then $b$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective], and $X^*$ is quasi-projective of finite type over $B$. Quasi-projective means a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$.

source.place: VIII Theorem 1.1, 4.1.1--4.2.13, 5.3.8--5.5.5 and Theorem 5.6.1, pp.85,117--129; X 1.3--1.4, pp.139--141 (the operations used in the relative proof). Finite-projective-space refinement uses the ample base in the last paragraph.

proof.text: Fix the saturated fan resolution rule once. Apply the general log-regular regularization tower to (X,M). It is equivariant because it is compatible with automorphisms; it is a normalized blowup tower with integral, regular, log regular source. The divisorial-structure theorem identifies the log structure with the boundary complement and makes its triviality locus dense and regular. Thus the tower is the identity off Z. The free-characteristic criterion identifies the resulting boundary as a normal crossings divisor. This constructs stage one without an excellent affine base assumption.

For stage two, stratify the strict transform of the original boundary by the number of local branches and blow its closed deepest stratum. Etale locally this is the ideal $(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ when that stratum meets $d$ branches. The coordinate-branch-drop lemma gives the following explicit calculation. On its $t_i$ chart the coordinates are $t_i$, $t_j/t_i$ for $j\ne i$ in that set, and the remaining parameters. The strict transform has at most $d-1$ of these branch equations; it has exactly that depth wherever it is nonempty at the old deepest stratum. The weak-family blowup lemma applied to the local branch family and the permissible-boundary lemma preserve regularity and normal crossings. Repeat on the strict transform: induction on its finite depth removes it after finitely many steps. The final boundary consists only of accumulated exceptional components and is strict normal crossings. Each center and its regular exceptional divisor are invariant; distinct irreducible components of a regular divisor are disjoint, so translates of each exceptional component are disjoint or equal. Subsequent equivariant blowups preserve this property of strict transforms. Thus the final boundary is G-strict. These centers are boundary monomial ideals; the displayed smooth charts identify the ordinary blowups with their saturated log blowups. All centers lie over Z.

On the regular pair now obtained, apply tame fixed-family transversality to the nontrivial subgroup fixed subschemes $X^H$. It gives the regularity and boundary normal-crossings hypotheses for every intersection, identifies intersections with fixed schemes of generated subgroups, and identifies their union with the nonfree locus. The weak-family blowup lemma therefore produces a finite permissible tower, blowing the union of minimal fixed intersections and then their strict transforms. Conjugation permutes this family, and the lemma's permutation compatibility makes every center and the tower G-equivariant. At its end every original fixed-scheme ideal is invertible and every strict transform is empty. The new boundary is the inverse image of the old boundary together with the nonfree locus. Off that boundary the tower is unchanged and the action is free.

For a geometric point with nonabelian inertia $H$, put $K=[H,H]\ne1$. The common G-equivariant tower of the preceding step makes the ideal of $X^K$ invertible. The factorization clause of the commutator blowup lemma factors that common tower through $\operatorname{Bl}_{X^K}X$ as an H-equivariant map. Its inertia-drop clause makes every upstairs inertia over that point a proper subgroup of H. Inertia over a point whose inertia was already abelian is a subgroup of it and stays abelian. Repeat the whole finite minimal-family tower, not an isolated H-center blowup. Along any geometric point lifted through successive rounds, every nonabelian inertia strictly decreases in order. Orders are initially at most $|G|$, so at most $|G|$ rounds suffice uniformly. The permissible and equivariant assertions from the preceding step persist; accumulated exceptional divisors remain G-strict by the same component argument as in stage two. This constructs stage three with abelian inertia and a free complement.

Write $(W,B)$ for the stage-three pair. Choose the strict inert affine surjective etale cover $U\to W$ of the rigidification-cover lemma, with enlarged very tame strict normal crossings boundary $\overline B_U$. Its hypotheses hold: W is regular with G-strict strict normal crossings boundary by stages two and three; W is Noetherian, separated and quasi-excellent because the normalized-tower lemma, applied to the composite of the first three towers on the Noetherian quasi-excellent normal separated X, makes every stage Noetherian and quasi-excellent and the composite projective, hence separated; and inertia is abelian with free complement by stage three. On the affine U the action is admissible. The very-tame log-quotient theorem gives a finite quotient $q:U\to Q$, its invariant fs log regular structure with boundary $q(\overline B_U)$, and the Kummer etale G-cover. This argument permits finitely many connected components of U.

Apply the same general regularization rule to the log regular quotient Q; no quasi-projective or excellent-base hypothesis is needed. Obtain a saturated log blowup tower $Q'\to Q$ with Q' regular and log regular; by the free-characteristic criterion its enlarged boundary is a normal crossings divisor, possibly not strict, which is all the Kummer lemma requires. Pull it back in fs log schemes along q. Kummer boundary restriction supplies stability under this pullback, the normalized-cover identification, and log regularity. The invariant-boundary Q-Cartier lemma applied to $B_U\subset\overline B_U$ shows that $D'=(h^{-1}q(B_U))_{\rm red}$ is a normal crossings union of components in Q'. Off q(B_U), q has trivial inertia and is etale by the Kummer lemma; regularity of this open quotient follows from the flat-under-regular lemma on local rings of this surjective etale cover. The resolution is therefore its identity there. Consequently the pulled-back cover is etale off D'. The boundary-restriction clause now removes the auxiliary components: with boundary $q'^{-1}D'$ the source is fs log regular and very tame. That boundary is exactly the inverse image of B_U. The normalized tower on U is the underlying tower of the pulled-back saturated log blowups, retaining ordered centers as in the rigidified-comparison lemma.

First compare two enlarged rigidifying boundaries on a fixed admissible regular pair. For any geometric point x take the completed strict local ring. Strict henselization and completion preserve Noetherian regular local rings; strict henselization and completion are faithfully flat. The rigidified-comparison lemma identifies the contracted pullback of either tower with its complete-local construction. The complete-local rigidification-comparison lemma makes those contracted towers equal. To recover their order before contraction, choose finitely many points S meeting the image of every nonempty center in both original finite towers, and include their finite G-orbits. On the disjoint union of the completed strict local schemes at S no stage contracts. Compare also on its disjoint union with the completed strict local scheme at x. The complete-local lemma applies to finite disjoint unions, so equality there respects the full synchronized order. Restricting back to x gives equality before contraction. Faithfully flat detection of ordered ideals in the descent lemma therefore proves equality of the two original towers, including all centers.

source.place: VIII Corollary 5.5.3, including the synchronization argument, pp.128--129

proof.text: For a strict inertia-preserving equivariant map of the original pairs, pull back a chosen enlarged rigidification. The rigidified-comparison lemma gives the strict quotient map and contracted scheme-pullback comparison. The preceding step removes the choice of auxiliary boundary, so the comparison depends only on the original pairs; identities and composition hold because they do so before forgetting the rigidification. Apply this to the two projections from $U\times_WU$. The two boundary choices there give the same ordered tower, and their comparisons agree on the triple fibre product. The normalized-tower descent lemma descends the centers and the tower from U to W, with its G-action. Log regularity and very tameness can be checked on this strict inert etale cover: characteristic monoids, strict local strata, and stabilizers are identified by its strictness and inertia isomorphisms. The inverse-image boundary descends as well. This is the global fourth stage.

Compose the four finite towers. Stages two and three have regular sources and hence are already normal, so their ordinary blowups are normalized blowups with the same centers. The normalized-tower lemma gives integrality, finite type, projectivity in the projective-bundle sense, and preservation of the common dense open. In stages one and two the centers lie above Z; in stage three they lie above the old boundary or nonfree locus; and stage four is the identity off the stage-three boundary. Thus the composite is the identity over $X\setminus(Z\cup F)$ and its boundary is exactly $b^{-1}(Z\cup F)$. The first-stage dense open is dense by the divisorial-structure theorem; intersecting with the given free dense open remains dense since X is integral. This also establishes birationality. Choosing the fixed resolution rule in the constructions gives the simultaneous choice required in the statement.

Suppose finally that X has a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_B$ with B affine Noetherian. Write it as a closed immersion into an open subscheme V of that projective space. V is quasi-compact, since projective space over B is Noetherian. The Proj twisting lemma supplies an ample invertible twist on V and closed-immersion restriction gives an ample invertible sheaf on X. The projective-bundle-to-H-projective lemma now embeds $X^*$ as a closed subscheme of some $\mathbf P^m_X$. The given locally closed immersion of X into $\mathbf P^n_B$ induces the same type of immersion $\mathbf P^m_X\to\mathbf P^m_B\times_B\mathbf P^n_B$ (base change of its open/closed factorization). Compose with the Segre closed immersion. This gives a locally closed immersion of $X^*$ into a finite projective space over B, as asserted; finite type follows also from finite type of the tower and the given X over B. No excellence hypothesis on B is used.
